summary: Hopkins County, KY tower announced in 1951 under a 99-year state forestry lease near Concord church; completion was expected, and it is now marked Removed, with no date.

facts.design: Steel tower, announced in 1951 as fifty feet high
facts.status_note: Marked Removed on the Forest Lookouts page; no source confirms completion, gives a removal date or describes the site today

events.note: Forestry division announced a 99-year lease and planned construction; tower expected to be ready in early November 1951, completion not confirmed

Charleston Tower, The Dawson Springs Progress, Oct. 3, 1957, quoted on Forest Lookouts

notes_for_editor: One 1951 newspaper announcement quoted on one site; nothing confirms the tower was finished or says when it came down. Two web searches found nothing about the tower or the lease. The 1951 item calls the ranger 'Major L. Brandon' and the 1957 item 'Ranger M. L. Brandon'; the story reports both without deciding they are the same man. The lessee is named in the source but left unnamed in the story as a private individual. The 50-foot height is the announced figure, so it is not recorded as a structure height. Record coordinates (37.4195, -87.5904) were not checked against the 3.6-miles-north-of-Manitou description.
